## Source-support finding

### F1 — Decision date presented as trial start date (claim 10)

Draft: “Before its maintenance team began the trial in September 2025 …”

Complete proposition: The maintenance team began the trial in September 2025.

Source: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”

Missing support: The source dates the decision, not explicitly the beginning of the eight-week trial. A source-compatible counterexample is a decision in September followed by an October start and completion before the December 4 note. All source statements could then be true while the draft’s start-date claim would be false. The contextual reading recorded initially in claim 10 therefore fails the strict counterexample test; claim 10 is unsupported at that precision.

Smallest supported repair: Replace “Before its maintenance team began the trial in September 2025, telephone reports and emails were stored separately” with “In September 2025, its maintenance team decided to trial the log. Previously, telephone reports and emails were stored separately.” This retains the supplied date and chronology without adding a start date. Alternatively, “Before the trial, telephone reports and emails were stored separately” removes only the unsupported dating precision but omits the supported decision date.

All other listed propositions pass the source-compatible-counterexample test. No causal software claim, cost saving, resident delight, completion-time improvement, invented scene, supplier comparison or universal endorsement is introduced.

## Quotation and translation findings

All three quotations exactly reproduce the supplied complete quotations. They retain Lind’s viewpoint, certainty, distinctive wording and preparation reservation. No translation was performed, so there are no translation findings. The introductory interpretation stays attributed to Lind and does not convert her experience into an objective measured result.

## Completion status

One unresolved source-support finding: F1, the unsupported September trial-start date. No unresolved translation findings. No source or draft changes made.

# Final source comparison

Scope: complete supplied source.md against complete supplied draft.md. Language: en_US; source and draft English. Applied the supplied Claims contract and quotation guidance. This is source comparison only; no editorial or mechanical assessment.

## Claim accounting

Each entry reconstructs the independently checkable proposition with its applicable scope and attribution. “Supported” means the supplied source does not permit a counterexample to that proposition under its ordinary contextual reading. Attributed wishes, judgments and advice are assessed as the speaker’s expressed position, not as independently demonstrated outcomes.

The heading does not claim all properties or all reports were included; the opening immediately supplies the two-building scope.

2. **Draft:** “Elm Quay Housing’s maintenance team tried a shared repair log in two buildings.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay’s maintenance team conducted a shared-repair-log trial in two buildings. **Source:** “its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings”; “The trial lasted eight weeks.” **Assessment:** Supported.

3. **Draft:** “to help staff on different shifts see the same information.” **Proposition:** The maintenance team’s purpose for that two-building trial was to let staff on different shifts see the same information. **Source:** “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.” **Assessment:** Supported as purpose, not a quantified result.

4. **Draft:** “Supervisor Maya Lind says the shared view helps.” **Proposition:** Maya Lind is a supervisor and says a shared view of repair reports helps her team. **Source:** “maintenance supervisor Maya Lind”; “Having one view of the reports helps us.” **Assessment:** Supported identity and attributed assessment; no stronger objective efficiency claim is made.

5. **Draft:** “but she would allow more preparation time before another trial.” **Proposition:** Lind’s favorable assessment is qualified by her preference for more preparation time if the trial were repeated. **Source:** “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.” **Assessment:** Supported; “more” retains the direction of her reservation, and the complete quotation later specifies an extra week.

6. **Draft:** “The team has yet to expand it.” **Proposition:** The team has not yet expanded the trial. **Source:** “The trial has not yet expanded.” **Assessment:** Supported; no future expansion is presented as settled.

7. **Draft:** “Published by Svale Systems.” **Proposition:** This case is supplier-published material, with Svale Systems as publisher. **Source:** Brief: “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems”; material: “approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.” **Assessment:** Supported as the required publication framing, without implying independent journalism.

8. **Draft:** “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay Housing manages 640 dwellings described as flats in the source. **Source:** “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.” **Assessment:** Supported; “apartments” is the en_US equivalent in this context.

9. **Draft:** “In September 2025, its maintenance team decided to trial the log.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay’s own maintenance team decided in September 2025 to trial the shared repair log. **Source:** “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.” **Assessment:** Supported; this states the decision date, not an invented precise trial start date.

10. **Draft:** “Previously, telephone reports and emails were stored separately.” **Proposition:** Before the shared-log trial, telephone reports and emails were kept separately. **Source:** “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.” **Assessment:** Supported.

11. **Draft:** “The team chose Svale Systems after testing whether its log could show the status of each repair.” **Proposition:** The maintenance team chose Svale Systems after testing the log’s ability to display the status of each repair. **Source:** “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.” **Assessment:** Supported. There is no claim of a supplier comparison, superiority, or guaranteed broader functionality.

12. **Draft:** “In an email interview, maintenance supervisor Maya Lind explained what the team wanted to change.” **Proposition:** Lind is Elm Quay’s maintenance supervisor, and her supplied remarks about what the team wanted came from an email interview. **Source:** “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind”; “All interviews occurred by email”; first quotation expresses the shift-information objective. **Assessment:** Supported identity, medium and characterization of the statement’s topic.

13. **Draft:** “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done.” **Proposition:** Lind said the team wanted the evening shift to see the morning shift’s completed actions. **Source:** Identical first sentence of the first usable quotation. **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim. This is a stated objective, not a measured finding that every shift saw every action.

14. **Draft:** “The categories were ours.” **Proposition:** Lind claimed ownership of the log categories for the customer’s team. **Source:** Identical clause in the first usable quotation; “The maintenance team designed its categories.” **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim; customer agency is preserved.

15. **Draft:** “Svale helped us put them into the log.” **Proposition:** Lind said Svale helped the maintenance team put its categories into the log. **Source:** Identical clause in the first usable quotation. **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim, with the pronoun referring to categories as in the source.

16. **Draft:** “The maintenance team designed the categories.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay’s maintenance team designed the categories used in the trial. **Source:** “The maintenance team designed its categories.” **Assessment:** Supported.

17. **Draft:** “and kept telephone reporting open for residents.” **Proposition:** The same maintenance team preserved telephone reporting for residents while trialing the log. **Source:** “and kept telephone reporting open for residents.” **Assessment:** Supported.

18. **Draft:** “Svale configured the log.” **Proposition:** Svale configured the trial log. **Source:** “Svale configured the log.” **Assessment:** Supported.

19. **Draft:** “and trained six staff members during two sessions.” **Proposition:** Svale trained six staff members over two sessions for the trial. **Source:** “and trained six staff during two sessions.” **Assessment:** Supported; neither individual session attendance nor training outcomes are invented.

20. **Draft:** “For Lind, the setup offered a lesson for future implementation.” **Proposition:** Lind drew advice for subsequent implementation from the time spent setting up the categories. **Source:** “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” **Assessment:** Supported characterization of her attributed interpretation. “Lesson” introduces no new external outcome or general prescription.

21. **Draft:** “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.” **Proposition:** Lind said her team spent more time agreeing on categories than entering the first reports. **Source:** Identical first sentence of second usable quotation. **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim. 23. **Draft:** “The trial lasted eight weeks.” **Proposition:** The shared-log trial lasted eight weeks. **Source:** “The trial lasted eight weeks.” **Assessment:** Supported.

24. **Draft:** “Elm Quay’s internal trial note, dated December 4, 2025.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay has an internal note concerning the trial dated December 4, 2025. **Source:** “Elm Quay’s internal trial note, 4 December 2025.” **Assessment:** Supported; date is reformatted without changing it.

26. **Draft:** “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial.” **Proposition:** For the trial’s report-to-assignment measure, the median was two working days. **Source:** “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial.” **Assessment:** Supported; endpoint, statistic, unit and period are preserved.

The grammatical comparison inherits “median,” “report to assignment” and “working days”; it is not a completion-time or calendar-day claim.

No causal relationship or workload equivalence is implied; the next sentence explicitly prevents both readings.

30. **Draft:** “the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay’s note explicitly declines to attribute the difference between the two report-to-assignment medians to the software. **Source:** “the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.” **Assessment:** Supported. This does not claim the software had no effect; it accurately preserves the absence of causal attribution.

31. **Draft:** “It contains no measurements of costs.” **Proposition:** The internal trial note contains no cost measurements. **Source:** “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” **Assessment:** Supported. The source’s unqualified statement that such measurements are absent entails their absence from the supplied note; this does not claim no costs occurred or no money was saved.

32. **Draft:** “It contains no measurements of ... resident satisfaction.” **Proposition:** The internal trial note contains no resident-satisfaction measurements. **Source:** “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” **Assessment:** Supported. This asserts absence of measurement, not absence of satisfaction or dissatisfaction.

33. **Draft:** “It contains no measurements of ... repair completion time.” **Proposition:** The internal trial note contains no repair-completion-time measurements. **Source:** “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” **Assessment:** Supported. The source also explicitly calls this her “actual, qualified assessment.”

37. **Draft:** “Having one view of the reports helps us.” **Proposition:** Lind says having one shared view of the repair reports helps her team. **Source:** Identical clause of third usable quotation. **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim as her judgment; no cost, speed, satisfaction or completion benefit is specified.

38. **Draft:** “but I would leave an extra week for preparation.” **Proposition:** Lind qualifies her favorable judgment by saying she would allow one additional week for preparation on a repeat trial. **Source:** Identical final clause of third usable quotation. **Assessment:** Supported and verbatim. 39. **Draft:** “The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” **Proposition:** Elm Quay’s team will decide on expansion after checking its categories’ suitability for larger repairs. **Source:** “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” **Assessment:** Supported. “Whether to expand” resolves the decision’s referent directly from the preceding source clause; it does not add a new criterion or imply expansion is assured.

## Findings

No source-support findings. The complete draft preserves the customer’s agency, the two-building trial’s scope, the count’s exclusions, the proper assignment-time endpoint, the different workloads and explicit absence of causal attribution. It preserves Lind’s reservation and the undecided expansion. No external comparison, unsupported scene, emotion, cost saving, resident-satisfaction result or completion-time result has been added.

Counterexample testing found no proposition that could be false while all supplied material remained true under its ordinary contextual reading. In particular, an unknown software effect remains possible in the source and draft; unmeasured outcomes remain unknown; Lind’s favorable judgment remains attributed rather than presented as a causal inference from the timing figures; and the title’s shared view does not imply portfolio-wide rollout.

## Quotation and translation findings

All three quotations reproduce their complete supplied English wording. Meaning, stance, certainty, distinctive wording and the preparation reservation are retained. All are correctly attributed to Lind and identified within the supplied email-interview context. No translation occurred, so translation findings are not applicable.

## Completion status

Complete: every factual and attributed claim in the complete draft, including heading, implied comparison, publication framing and link destination, accounted for above. Unresolved source-support findings: none. Unresolved translation findings: none. No repair proposed or needed.
